title: Research Engineer, AI (Entry-Level)
reason: Stack +55; Synergy +18; Title fit +6; Entry +15; Exp fit +10; US +10
description_preview:
Company Overview
Orbis is a technology company that delivers sovereign intelligence and decision capabilities to the United States Government and its allies. We convert complex information and operational systems into decisive outcomes, giving public institutions and critical enterprises the tools to move faster, see clearer, and act first in an increasingly contested world.
We are not a consulting firm and not a systems integrator. Every Orbis team is built around practitioners who have operated at the mission edge, and every engagement is judged on one thing: whether it produces working capability, not slide decks. Solutions forged from experience; that is how we build, and it is how we hire.
Job Summary
Support applied research across the Orbis AI focus areas — agentic AI, knowledge representation, dynamic ontologies, autonomous analysis, and high-performance analytics — working alongside senior research engineers on questions with real product stakes. You will reproduce baselines, build evaluation datasets and harnesses, run experiments, and write up what actually happened. This role exists to bring strong early-career engineers into applied AI research and grow them toward owning a research area.
Travel
: Occasional, up to 10%, for conferences, training, and team collaboration.
Key Responsibilities
Reproduce baselines and published methods, and document precisely where your results diverge from what was reported.
Build and maintain evaluation datasets and harnesses, including cases that capture known failure modes.
Run experiments designed with senior research engineers, keeping records complete enough that someone else can rerun them.
Perform error analysis — characterize what the system got wrong and why, and report it without smoothing it over.
Implement well-scoped prototype components with design direction and code review from senior engineers.
Summarize relevant literature and open-source work, and explain how it bears on the question at hand.
Write up results, negative results included, and present them in team research reviews.
Travel occasionally, up to 10%, for conferences, training, and team collaboration.
Required Qualifications
0-2 years of professional experience
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related technical field, or equivalent demonstrated ability
Solid programming fundamentals in Python, with code you can walk us through and defend
Working understanding of machine learning and LLM fundamentals — evaluation basics, prompting, embeddings, and retrieval — from coursework, projects, internships, or professional work
Ability to read a technical paper and explain what it claims, how it was evaluated, and where it might not hold
Intellectual honesty about results, including the ones that undercut a hypothesis you liked
Willingness to travel occasionally, up to 10%
Desired Qualifications
Research experience from a thesis, lab, internship, or open-source project
Hands-on project experience with retrieval-augmented generation, agent frameworks, or fine-tuning
Exposure to graph databases, ontologies, or information extraction
Experience with experiment tracking and evaluation tooling such as notebooks, dataset construction, or scoring pipelines
Exposure to containerized environments (Docker) and cloud or GPU compute
Interest in OSINT, intelligence, or investigative research workflows
Physical Requirements
Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
Participation in virtual and in-person meetings
Ability to attend planned meetings and/or work in classified spaces for extended periods within the specified work regions
Travel: Occasional, up to 10%, for conferences, training, and team collaboration.
Orbis Benefits
Beyond the opportunity to work alongside practitioners who have operated at the mission edge, joining Orbis means real ownership over outcomes that matter; the chance to build technology that gives the United States Government and its allies a genuine decision advantage, not just another dashboard. From competitive retirement matching to a PTO policy that encourages real time off, we're committed to creating an environment where our team can do their best work and still have a life outside of it.
Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to meet the diverse needs of our employees and their families. A full list of benefits is shared with candidates following an initial conversation with our HR team, so you'll have a clear picture of the support and resources available to you as part of the Orbis team.
Orbis Locations
Orbis works in whatever arrangement the mission requires. Depending on the role, that might mean five days a week on a customer site, full-time in one of our offices, a hybrid schedule, or fully remote work; our team is spread across 25 states and four countries to match. We make sure every team member has the tools and access needed to do the work, wherever that work happens.
Travel is common across many Orbis roles, particularly those supporting customer missions in the field.
Orbis is headquartered in McLean, VA, with additional office locations in Taipei, Taiwan, and Canberra, Australia.
Orbis is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We are committed to providing a work environment free of discrimination and harassment, and we make employment decisions based on merit,
qualifications, and business need. Orbis does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable law.
Orbis complies with all applicable equal opportunity and non-discrimination laws in every jurisdiction in which we operate. Reasonable accommodation is available to applicants and employees with disabilities upon request.

We are one of the fastest-growing vertical SaaS companies in history, and we are just getting started. EvenUp is backed by top VCs, including Bessemer Venture Partners, Bain Capital Ventures, SignalFire, and Lightspeed. We are looking to expand our team with talented, driven, and collaborative individuals who seek to have a lasting impact. Learn more at www.evenuplaw.com.
Machine Learning Engineer
We're looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to join our ML team at EvenUp. You'll develop and deploy models that power Piai™, our proprietary claims-intelligence platform, with a focus on machine learning, natural-language processing, and generative AI.
Working alongside senior ML engineers, data scientists, and legal subject-matter experts, you'll turn raw legal and medical data into production-ready models that directly improve outcomes for personal-injury clients.
What You'll Do
Explore, implement, and benchmark ML, NLP, and generative AI methods - including LLM fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation, and document understanding.
Clean, annotate, and transform structured and unstructured case data, and build reusable datasets and data loaders.
Design experiments, run A/B tests, analyze results, and communicate findings to product and engineering teams.
Help integrate models into our production systems, partnering with ML platform engineers on testing, monitoring, and scaling.
Pair with product managers, legal analysts, and software engineers to translate real problems into ML solutions and measurable improvements.
Stay current with research in LLMs, representation learning, and prompt engineering, and share what you learn with the team.
What You Bring
B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Data Science, Statistics, Computational Linguistics, or a related field.
Solid grounding in ML fundamentals - supervised and unsupervised learning, evaluation metrics, overfitting and regularization.
Hands-on experience with NLP or generative AI techniques - transformers, embeddings, sequence-to-sequence models, or LLMs.
Proficiency in Python and ML/NLP libraries such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, Hugging Face, or spaCy.
Familiarity with SQL and basic data engineering concepts - ETL, versioned datasets, notebooks.
Strong analytical thinking, clear communication, and eagerness to learn and iterate quickly in a fast-moving startup.
Ability to work hybrid (3 days your choice) in our San Francisco or Toronto, Canada office.
Nice to Have
Exposure to cloud platforms (AWS, GCP).
Experience with experiment-tracking tools (Weights & Biases, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, MLflow).
Familiarity with containerized deployment (Docker, Kubernetes).
Experience in a high-growth startup environment.

Choice of medical, dental, and vision insurance plans for you and your family.
Additional insurance coverage options for life, accident, or critical illness.

10 US observed holidays, and Canadian statutory holidays by province.
A home office stipend.
401(k) for US-based employees and RRSP for Canada-based employees.

Hubs in San Francisco and Toronto.

Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience
2+ years of experience developing and deploying web applications

Hands-on experience with both user-facing web applications and backend services or APIs

PostgresSQL or other relational database experience modeling
Python, including FastAPI or Django or Flask
Experience with front-end frameworks such as React, Vite, or Vue and UX concepts
Clinical research systems such as electronic data capture tools, clinical trial management, protocol tools, case report forms, or Veeva Vault
Graph DB relationship mapping, traversal, and cypher querying knowledge
AI Agent crafting and support experience is a plus

description_preview:
Job Description
About ClearConnect Solutions
At ClearConnect Solutions, an Acrisure company, we believe there’s a story in your data, and we help our clients see it. We specialize in cutting-edge, data-driven technology solutions for fleet insurers, underwriters, and policyholders. From real-time risk score monitoring, automated Motor Vehicle Report (MVR) services, and screening platforms to advanced telematics and route optimization, our software empowers the transportation and insurance industries to mitigate risk, streamline compliance, and build safer driver workforces.
We are expanding our software development capabilities and looking for a dynamic Software Developer.
Job Summary
The Software Developer designs, develops, tests, and supports scalable, cloud-native applications across the full software development lifecycle. This role builds containerized Spring Boot and MySQL solutions, modern front-end applications using Nuxt.js and Vue.js, REST APIs, and AWS serverless services. The developer works closely with Scrum team members to estimate work, identify risks, prioritize development tasks, and deliver secure, stable, and user-focused solutions.
Responsibilities
Full Stack Development: Develop Docker, Spring Boot, and MySQL solutions using modern front-end application patterns, including static applications, server-side rendering, and single-page applications built with Nuxt.js and Vue.js.
API Development: Design and develop containerized REST API applications using the Spring Boot framework.
Cloud-Native Services: Build AWS serverless services when appropriate, using technologies that may include API Gateway, Amazon SQS, AWS Lambda, AWS Glue, AWS Step Functions, and Amazon Cognito.
Requirements Delivery: Interpret and implement stated software requirements while identifying technical dependencies and considerations.
Scrum Planning: Provide development estimates and communicate constraints, risks, and potential liabilities as part of the Scrum process.
Work Prioritization: Plan and prioritize development tasks to meet project objectives and customer-initiated deadlines.
Testing & Quality: Design test protocols that provide a high level of confidence in application stability, usability, security, and overall quality.
CI/CD & Build Tools: Use CI/CD pipelines and modern build tools, including NPM, Yarn, Docker, AWS SAM, and Gradle.
Required Qualifications
2+ years' experience with an object-oriented programming language such as Java or C#, along with Python and JavaScript.
Familiarity with Java Spring Boot, JHipster, or similar application-development frameworks.
Familiarity with AWS cloud development and cloud-native application patterns.
Demonstrated ability and interest in learning new systems, frameworks, and programming languages quickly.
Ability to consistently produce high-quality work while balancing multiple priorities and deadlines
Strong collaboration, teamwork, interpersonal, and communication skills.
Ability to meet stated customer-initiated deadlines.
Ability to maintain confidentiality and demonstrate professionalism in all Acrisure-related activities.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with React.js and/or Vue.js using the Nuxt.js framework.
Experience with CSS frameworks such as Bootstrap, Vuetify, or Tailwind CSS.
Experience with Apache Spark and the PySpark library.
Hands-on experience with Docker, MySQL, REST APIs, CI/CD pipelines, NPM, Yarn, AWS SAM, or Gradle.
Experience with AWS services such as API Gateway, Amazon SQS, AWS Lambda, AWS Glue, AWS Step Functions, and Amazon Cognito.
Pay Details:
The base compensation range for this position is $85,000 - $85,000. This range reflects Acrisure's good faith estimate at the time of this posting. Placement within the range will be based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to skills, experience, qualifications, location, and internal equity.
Candidates should be comfortable with an on-site presence to support collaboration, team leadership, and cross-functional partnership.
Why Join Us:
At Acrisure, we’re building more than a business, we’re building a community where people can grow, thrive, and make an impact. Our benefits are designed to support every dimension of your life, from your health and finances to your family and future.
Making a lasting impact on the communities it serves, Acrisure has pledged more than $22 million through its partnerships with Corewell Health Helen DeVos Children's Hospital in Grand Rapids, Michigan, UPMC Children's Hospital in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania and Blythedale Children's Hospital in Valhalla, New York.
Employee Benefits
We also offer our employees a comprehensive suite of benefits and perks, including:
Physical Wellness: Comprehensive medical insurance, dental insurance, and vision insurance; life and disability insurance; fertility benefits; wellness resources; and paid sick time.
Mental Wellness: Generous paid time off and holidays; Employee Assistance Program (EAP); and a complimentary Calm app subscription.
Financial Wellness: Immediate vesting in a 401(k) plan; Health Savings Account (HSA) and Flexible Spending Account (FSA) options; commuter benefits; and employee discount programs.
Family Care: Paid maternity leave and paid paternity leave (including for adoptive parents); legal plan options; and pet insurance coverage.
… and so much more!

description_preview:
Summary
About the Product
Concierge is Guidewire's omnichannel AI agent for P&C carriers. It answers the phone when a policyholder has just had an accident, takes first notice of loss, asks the questions a good adjuster would ask, and writes a clean claim into ClaimCenter. It runs in production today with real carriers and real policyholders, not as a demo.
Two things make this harder than a typical chatbot. First, it has synchronous voice: latency is a product requirement, not a metric on a dashboard. Second, FNOL is a regulated event where the quality of the intake determines the eventual cost of the claim. A missed question early is a bigger loss reserve later.
The Role
You will build, evaluate, and harden the agent itself: the orchestration, the context it sees, the tools it can call, and the evals that tell us whether a change made it better or just different.
Our rollout philosophy is a dimmer, not a light switch. We widen the agent's autonomy one notch at a time, and every notch has to be earned with evidence. Much of your work is producing that evidence, then acting on what it says.
Job Description
What you'll do
Own end-to-end slices of the agent: prompt and context architecture, retrieval over policy and coverage data, tool and API calls into core claims systems, and handoff to a human when the agent should stop.
Build and run the eval loop, golden sets, trajectory evaluation, LLM-as-judge, error analysis on real production call traces, and make it the thing that gates releases.
Drive containment and resolution rates up without trading away accuracy, and instrument the system well enough that we can tell which of the two moved.
Work directly on the voice path: turn-taking, interruption, latency budgets, and the telephony layer underneath (LiveKit, SIP).
Sit in on carrier calls and listen to recordings. The best fixes usually come from hearing where the conversation went sideways, not from reading the logs.
What We're Looking For
Building and deploying AI applications. You've shipped an LLM application that real users depend on, and you know that the hard part is that the output is not predictable. You're fluent in the building blocks LLMs, context engineering, RAG, agentic workflows, and you have real ML and deep learning depth underneath that fluency. Most importantly, you know how to make an unpredictable system behave predictably enough to trust: disciplined evals, error analysis, and statistical measurement rather than vibes and a handful of spot checks.
Software engineering fundamentals. You can reason about cost, latency, reliability, and scalability as tradeoffs rather than goals, and you know which ones you're making. You've designed data stores and distributed systems, you write tests, and you take security and privacy seriously while advocating CI/CD process automation. We handle claims data, recorded calls, and PII under carrier and regulatory scrutiny.
Using coding agents. You work with coding agents daily and you're good at it: managing their context, deciding when a spec is worth writing and when it isn't, giving them verifiers so they can close their own loops, and knowing when to intervene versus leave them alone. You also keep changing how you work as the tooling changes, rather than settling into a 2025 workflow.
Shaping the build. You won't be handed a finished spec. You'll be in the room where we decide what the agent should do next, which means you need product sense and enough insurance context to argue about it. You'll know when to put an MVP in front of a carrier next week and when a claims workflow demands that we slow down and get it right the first time.
Underneath all four: you keep learning. This field looks different every six months and we expect to keep changing our minds.
Nice to have
Real-time or streaming voice systems (ASR, TTS, telephony, SBC/SIPREC)
Insurance, claims, or another regulated domain where being wrong has a cost attached
Experience building internal eval or observability tooling other engineers actually adopted.
Experience in Machine learning principles, or have experience in model experimentations, training and deploying models in Productions.
Experience in P&C Insurance or exposure to Guidewire products and services.
Prompt or pipeline optimization frameworks (DSPy, GEPA) applied to a production system
How To Apply
Send a short note about something you shipped where the model's unpredictability was the central problem, and what you did about it. We care more about that than about a list of frameworks.

title: Software Engineer

description_preview:
About Us
Mintive helps companies put agents to work safely. We exist to help companies do more of their work with agents, and we build the infrastructure that makes a company's own work runnable by them. That has to start from trust. Our first product is an MCP gateway that gives those agents governed access to company data and tools.
Before agents can touch Slack, GitHub, Jira, Snowflake, internal databases, or production systems, you need to know what they can reach, what they did, and why they were allowed to do it. Most people carry far more permissions than any single task needs. If an agent uses your token directly, it inherits all of them. Our gateway product scopes that access down to exactly what an agent needs to do its job and captures the data flows and audit logs security teams need. From there we are building the rest of the agent stack: connectors, monitoring, sandboxing, long-running agents, and memory, with the goal of becoming the system a company's work runs on.
We work in person in the San Francisco Bay Area. The structure is flat and the market moves fast, so you have a lot of latitude over what you work on and how.
We are AI-native. Everyone uses Claude and Codex every day, and we have more agents than employees. They run in Slack alongside the team and handle sales, marketing, deal ops, and engineering on the same gateway we sell to customers, and we are building an entire company operating system around them.
Since launching in February 2026, we have grown to 50+ paying customers, with strong inbound demand. Customers include Coursera, Arlo, and Braze. We are backed by Cowboy Ventures and Coatue, with angels including Frederic Kerrest (Okta), Michael Grinich (WorkOS), Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Dean, and Scott Belsky. Our founders are machine learning experts from Stanford, Berkeley, and CMU, with applied research at Google Brain and Waymo, and one co-founded Coursera.
The Job
You will own features end to end, from conception to production, across our gateway infrastructure, enterprise deployments, and agentic systems. The work leans backend and infra, but nothing is off limits: when the product needs a better UI you build it, and when a connector breaks during a security review you fix it.
Claude and Codex are your primary working environment, and you use a fleet of agents to move faster than a team this size has any right to. Agents write much of the code and review PRs, so your real job is the judgment they cannot make: shaping the problem, making architecture, product, and UX calls, hardening enterprise paths, designing connectors, protecting security-sensitive surfaces, and catching generated code that is quietly wrong. Roles are blurred and we ship within hours, and you will learn directly from the founders and from customers.
We hire across levels, from strong early-career builders to seasoned engineers, and we set level and pay to match. What matters most is judgment, range, and how fast you ship.
About You
You are a builder with a track record of shipping to real users, whether that is a product, an internal tool, an open-source project, or a serious side project. You ship, then iterate, without waiting for specs or approvals.
You have strong fundamentals and learn fast. How quickly you pick things up matters as much as years of experience.
You care about product value and customer needs over technical purity.
You take infra seriously. You think about blast radius, trust boundaries, and what happens when your code is in the path of every customer's agents.
You can read unfamiliar code, reason from first principles, and explain your tradeoffs.
You are comfortable across the stack (TypeScript, Python, CockroachDB), or you pick up new languages, protocols, and domains fast.
You are excited to build with agents, and to learn when they help and when they hide a problem.
You already build with AI every day and want room to move without heavy process.
Nice to have:
Developer-facing products, protocol or gateway work, or infrastructure at scale.
Background in security, identity, or permission systems.
Contributions to open source, MCP servers, or agentic frameworks.
Design sensibility: engineers who care about design, designers who think about infrastructure.
What we offer:
Competitive compensation and meaningful equity.
Unusual scope and ownership of features that ship to enterprise customers.
Building and deploying agents on the same platform we sell.
Direct access to the founders, customer context, and product direction, with mentorship as you grow.
Health benefits, on a team that puts family and health first.

https://www.mintmcp.com/hiring/mcp

As a Software Manufacturing Test Engineer, you will build, scale, and maintain the software that drives our manufacturing test systems. You will bridge low-level hardware control with high-level test automation by writing robust, reliable production code in Python and C# targeting Linux/Unix (and ideally NixOS) runtime environments.

Torch Technologies is currently seeking a highly motivated
Modeling and Simulation
(M&S) Engineer/Analyst
to support the analysis of high-fidelity tactical missile systems models and simulations on Redstone Arsenal. The ideal candidate has a strong quantitative background and demonstrated ability to independently assess system performance data. The candidate will develop and execute analysis studies, process and evaluate large Monte Carlo simulation datasets, identify factors driving system behavior, and communicate technical findings to engineer teams and government. A successful candidate is a critical thinker capable of taking an engineering problem or performance question, developing a structured analytical approach, determining the data required to answer questions, assessing the validity of results, and providing clear conclusions and recommendations.
Job Duties
Develop Python and MATLAB tools to automate data extraction and reduction, statistical analysis, and visualizations.
Perform detailed analysis of sensors algorithms and end-to-end simulation system performance.
Execute and analyze Monte Carlo parametric, sensitivity, and uncertainty studies to characterize system behavior across nominal and off-nominal conditions.
Apply sound engineering judgment and critical thinking to investigate unexpected results, inconsistent data, outliers, and model input/output issues.
Prepare clear, technically rigorous reports, briefing charts, and visualizations and present findings to engineering teams and government customers.

US Citizenship.

Demonstrated ability to independently define an analytical problem, develop a logical analysis approach, identify required data, execute the study, and communicate conclusions.
Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills, including the ability to evaluate assumptions, question results, identify data limitations, and distinguish meaningful findings from artifacts or unsupported conclusions.

Active Secret security clearance.

: Watertown, SD
Terex Utilities is a global leader in manufacturing aerial devices and digger derricks for the electric utility industry. With a focus on supporting customers across North America, the company offers a comprehensive range of services, including manufacturing, distribution, service, training, and parts support. Committed to innovation and reliable equipment, Terex Utilities delivers solutions designed to meet the unique challenges faced by utility professionals. What You'll Do
This is a full-time, on-site role located in Watertown, SD for an Electrical and Software Control Engineer specializing in Real-Time Control Systems. In this role, you will design and implement electrical and software control systems, develop and test software for real-time applications, and integrate electrical components and systems for utility equipment. Responsibilities will also include troubleshooting and debugging system issues, collaborating with cross-functional teams, and contributing to the development of innovative, reliable solutions.
This position will provide support for new product development surrounding unit controls, troubleshooting and current product maintenance. This person is required to become a subject matter expert around our current and new control and hydraulic systems.
What You'll Bring
Proficiency in Electrical Engineering and Electrical Design
3 Plus years’ Experience in Software Development and Software Design
Strong understanding of electrical/electronic components and its application in control systems
Ability to troubleshoot and debug complex systems
Strong team collaboration and communication skills
Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Software Engineering, Computer Science, or related field is preferred.
Experience with real-time control systems or utility equipment is a plus
Experience with Danfoss Plus+1 software is a plus.
Experience with Codesys software is a plus.
Knowledge of industry standards and safety practices relevant to the utility sector

Job Description
The Extended Reality (XR) Developer is responsible for designing, developing, deploying, and maintaining immersive applications and simulations using Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR), and Mixed Reality (MR) technologies. This position translates skills-based learning objectives and technical requirements into functional, engaging XR applications and interactive experiences that support faculty and students.
The XR Developer collaborates with faculty, instructional designers, project managers, Technical Artists, and engineering teams to develop scalable XR solutions using technologies such as Unity and/or Unreal Engine, WebXR, and related platforms. Responsibilities include software development, prototyping, user interaction design, AI integration, testing, optimization, troubleshooting, and deployment across VR headsets, desktop, browser-based, and LMS environments.
The position also contributes to the development of reusable frameworks, tools, workflows, and coding standards while researching and implementing emerging XR and AI technologies. Additionally, the XR Developer provides technical guidance and training to stakeholders and assists with the setup, configuration, maintenance, troubleshooting, and deployment of XR devices.
The Target Hiring Range for the position is $75,643 - 86,990.40
The final salary offer will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications and experience.
Essential Functions
The employee will demonstrate TSTC’s Core Values of
Excellence, Accountability, Service, and Integrity
with internal and external stakeholders, customers, students, and community members.
XR Application Development
Designs, develops, prototypes, deploys, and maintains immersive applications and simulations using Unity and/or Unreal Engine, and related XR technologies. Translates skills-based learning objectives, user needs, and technical requirements into functional, engaging, and accessible XR applications. Develops scalable XR applications, prototypes, frameworks, and reusable components that support organizational XR initiatives. Develops immersive user interactions, navigation, input systems, spatial interfaces, object manipulation, physics-based interactions, and other application behaviors appropriate to XR environments. Integrates AI technologies, including AI-driven avatars, conversational agents, and other intelligent systems, into immersive applications and experiences. Develops and deploys simulations compatible with existing XR platforms, devices, and applications. Conducts comprehensive testing and debugging throughout the development lifecycle to identify and resolve issues related to functionality, performance, compatibility, and user experience. Optimizes applications for performance, usability, scalability, and compatibility across target platforms. Troubleshoots and resolves application issues, including performance bottlenecks, software bugs, and device-specific challenges. Applies appropriate accessibility and usability principles to immersive experiences.
LMS & Web-Based XR Integration
Develops browser-based XR experiences using HTML, JavaScript, WebXR, and related web technologies. Collaborates with stakeholders and engineering teams to integrate XR experiences with existing Learning Management Systems (LMS) and web-based platforms. Develops and maintains reusable web-based XR frameworks, prototypes, and integration processes. Tests, troubleshoots, and optimizes browser-based XR applications for compatibility, performance, and usability. Supports integration of XR applications with LMS platforms and related learning technologies for authentication, launch, progress tracking, completion, assessment, and reporting.
Collaboration & Technical Documentation
Collaborates with instructional designers, faculty, subject matter experts, project managers, and engineering teams to define requirements and develop effective XR solutions. Collaborates with Technical Artists and other XR team members to integrate 3D assets and interactive content into XR applications. Partners with Application Engineering, AI Engineering, and Data Engineering to support the integration of XR applications with broader AI and technology initiatives. Establishes, documents, and maintains coding standards, development guidelines, workflows, and best practices. Documents code, architecture, design decisions, development processes, and technical solutions to support collaboration and knowledge sharing. Designs and implements application architecture, interfaces, APIs, and integration patterns needed to connect XR applications with enterprise platforms, AI services, data sources, and other systems.
Training & Technical Support
Provides training and technical guidance to faculty, instructional designers, staff, and other stakeholders on XR applications, technologies, and best practices. Consults with geographically distributed stakeholders to support the effective implementation and use of XR solutions. Assists with the setup, configuration, deployment, maintenance, troubleshooting, and inventory management of XR devices and equipment.
Research & Innovation

Stays current with evolving XR platforms, development tools, frameworks, standards, and industry practices. This role helps the scientists who build and operate QuEra's neutral-atom quantum computers program those machines effectively. You will work closely with physicists and control stack engineers. You'll help machine teams turn new experiments into working programs, keep the toolchain reliable as our hardware evolves, and drive its integration with our control system. Work with control stack engineers on integrating compiled programs with our control system. This includes defining and evolving the program representation passed between the compiler and the control system, keeping the two in sync across releases, and debugging problems that span both.
Turn user problems into minimal reproducible reports, regression tests and focused fixes, and work with the compiler team on larger language or IR changes.
Find and fix performance problems in program compilation and execution, such as compile time, program size and timing correctness.
Write and maintain user-facing documentation, tutorials, example programs and agent skills that make it easier for physicists to write correct programs.

Strong Python skills, including type hints, packaging and testing (pytest).
Enjoys building tools for, and working closely with, scientists who are not professional software developers. Clear written and verbal communication.
Experience working across team boundaries: agreeing on interfaces, coordinating changes between components and debugging problems that span several systems.
Experience debugging unfamiliar code and reducing complex failures to minimal reproductions.
Familiarity with the full software lifecycle: version control, code review, testing, CI/CD, logging, profiling, debugging and documentation.

description_preview:
About Elveo
Elveo is what happens when two pioneers in direct-to-device (D2D) communications join forces. Elveo brings together a combined 20 years of expertise to close the coverage gap for more than 50 mobile network operators (MNOs) and major distribution partners operating in 60+ countries worldwide.
That heritage and our technology powers what we call ‘elevated intelligence’ — a new approach that processes and adapts on orbit, delivering voice and data services straight to mobile users, IoT devices and machines across enterprise, government and humanitarian sectors worldwide.
As a team, we’re on a mission to deliver powerful compute and connectivity directly to individuals and objects everywhere on Earth.
Join us, and become part of a globally inclusive company that is transforming satellite communications from a niche service to an essential global infrastructure, and democratizing connectivity for billions worldwide.
Ready to take the next step? Join us.
About The Role
The Firmware Engineer at Elveo will develop the bare-metal and RTOS firmware that runs on the microcontrollers throughout our satellites — in the D2D communications payload and across the spacecraft bus. This role sits squarely between our Flight Software and Electrical Engineering teams: you will bring up new boards alongside the engineers who designed them, write the drivers and control loops that make that hardware useful, and define the interfaces that our Linux-based flight software uses to command and monitor it. The firmware will be developed and tested on lab hardware and on our "flatsat," a satellite prototype that simulates orbit operations, before it flies.
We build spacecraft fast! So, the ideal candidate enjoys taking a board from first power-on to flight-ready firmware on rapid timelines, and is equally comfortable reading a schematic, probing a bus with a logic analyzer, and reviewing a pull request. Firmware on orbit can only be fixed over a radio link, so we value engineers who design for robustness and recoverability from the start. This is a small team, so you will work alongside experienced engineers and take ownership of systems early.
Experience with satellites is not a requirement for this position. If you've shipped firmware for robotics, automotive, drones, medical devices, industrial controls, or similar, you'll find much of your experience translates directly. Title, scope, and compensation scale with experience.
Core Responsibilities
You Will Design, Develop, And Test Embedded Firmware For Microcontroller-based Subsystems Across The Spacecraft, Including Payload Control, Power, And Attitude Sensing And Actuation Electronics. This Includes
Developing bare-metal and RTOS firmware for microcontrollers, including device drivers, peripheral configuration, interrupt handling, and hardware abstraction layers.
Partnering with Electrical Engineering through schematic and design reviews, board bring-up, and debug of new hardware revisions.
Implementing communication with satellite devices and electronics using CAN, I2C, SPI, UART, RS-422, RS-485, and other protocols.
Defining and implementing the command, telemetry, and data interfaces between microcontroller firmware and Elveo's flight software.
Building bootloaders and firmware update mechanisms that can be safely exercised over a low-bandwidth radio link, with fallback images and recovery paths.
Designing for fault tolerance on orbit: watchdogs, brown-out and reset handling, memory protection and error detection, and graceful degradation.
Debugging hardware/firmware integration issues using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, JTAG/SWD debuggers, and other lab equipment.
Developing unit, hardware-in-the-loop, and flatsat tests for firmware, and integrating them into our CI pipelines.
Participating in design and code reviews, and documenting firmware designs, interfaces, and test procedures.
Supporting spacecraft integration, environmental testing, and on-orbit operations as needed.
Basic Qualifications
Proficiency in C for embedded systems, demonstrated through professional work, significant academic/personal projects, or open-source contributions.
Experience developing firmware for microcontrollers (e.g., ARM Cortex-M), including drivers for on-chip peripherals and external devices over SPI, I2C, UART, ethernet, CAN , etc.
Hands-on board bring-up and debug: reading schematics and datasheets, and using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and JTAG/SWD debuggers.
Experience designing interrupt-driven, real-time firmware, either bare-metal or on an RTOS.
Experience writing automated tests for firmware you build and working with Git and CI/CD.
A bachelor's degree or higher in Computer, Electrical, Software, Aerospace, or related engineering field, or equivalent practical experience.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience writing bootloaders and in-field or over-the-air firmware update systems.
Experience working in small teams with a high degree of project ownership
Familiarity with radiation effects on electronics and their mitigations (e.g., EDAC/ECC, memory scrubbing, latch-up protection, redundancy).
Familiarity with embedded Linux and how microcontroller firmware interfaces with a Linux host.
Experience with FPGAs or mixed-signal electronics, including ADC/DAC interfacing.
Experience developing and testing hardware for SmallSats / CubeSats.
Experience with hardware-in-the-loop integration and testing.
Scripting experience in Python for test automation and lab tooling.

1158. Individuals who do not meet these criteria must be eligible to obtain the necessary authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

Travelers Data Engineering team constructs pipelines that contextualize and provide easy access to data by the entire enterprise. description_preview:
The Digital Consumer team powers digital experiences and engagement to enhance the lives of millions of people every day through connected care. We build, deliver and manage a portfolio of data management platforms and mobile offerings in support of our core businesses. We thrive on simple and elegant architecture and agility. You’ll be immersed in a dynamic high-growth environment and empowered to excel, take informed risks, and drive ingenuity across the enterprise.
Location - San Diego, US (hybrid)
Let’s talk about the team and you:
As an iOS Engineer, you will be part of a highly collaborative team working on modern mobile technologies in the growing digital health space. We’re a team of engineers, designers, and product professionals who are passionate about creating meaningful experiences that help people around the world breathe easier.
You will be part of a team that partners closely with UX designers, product managers, and platform engineers to build and evolve shared UI foundations used throughout our digital consumer experiences. You will also collaborate with product teams to ensure these foundations enable the delivery of high-quality customer experiences across our mobile applications.
You will work closely with talented engineers, designers, product managers, architects, and stakeholders to deliver industry-leading mobile applications while helping establish patterns and components that can be leveraged across teams.
Let’s Talk About Responsibilities
Responsible for developing high-quality iOS applications and shared mobile components
Contribute to the design, implementation, and evolution of reusable UI components and shared mobile frameworks
Partner closely with UX designers to translate design patterns into scalable, accessible, and maintainable implementation
Drive consistency, quality, and usability across our mobile applications through shared components and best practices
Collaborate with other engineers and product owners to identify software solutions to complex problems in our industry
Advocate for accessibility, performance, and developer experience when building shared solutions
Collaborate with engineers across teams, including Android counterparts, to encourage consistency and continuous improvement of shared mobile capabilities
Take a quality-first approach to software development by producing unit tests and automating functional testing wherever possible
Leverage modern development tools, including AI-assisted engineering workflows, to improve productivity, code quality, and team effectiveness
Conduct code reviews with other developers
Support and mentor other engineers through collaboration, code reviews, and knowledge sharing
Participate in technical interviews
Let’s Talk About Qualifications And Experience
You must be a seasoned iOS developer, with at least 3 years of mobile development experience
Hands-on experience developing apps in Swift for at least 3 years
Experience designing and architecting iOS applications and understanding various design patterns
Experience with the use of Continuous Integration and automated testing frameworks
Experience working with SwiftUI and modern iOS development practice
Experience collaborating with designers and cross-functional product teams
Familiarity with accessibility standards and inclusive design principles
Experience working with peripherals, wearables, and Bluetooth is desirable
Master’s Degree in Computer Science or related discipline with 3+ years of experience; or Bachelor’s degree with 5+ years of experience in design and development
2+ years of experience making a significant individual contribution to real-world software development
Preferred Qualifications
Experience building reusable UI components, frameworks, or shared libraries
Experience contributing to or implementing a Design System
Experience working with modular architectures and Swift Package Manage
Experience collaborating with Android engineers to deliver consistent cross-platform experiences
Let’s Talk About What You Can Expect
A supportive environment that focuses on people development, collaboration, and engineering excellence
Opportunity to influence shared mobile foundations used across multiple products and teams
Work closely with engineers, designers, and product teams to solve meaningful customer problems
Exposure to modern mobile development practices, tooling, and AI-assisted engineering workflows
Work with global teams and share new ideas
Be supported both inside and outside of the work environment
The opportunity to build products that have a direct impact on people’s lives
Why join us
At Resmed, you’ll be part of a mission driven company focused on improving health and quality of life. This role offers high visibility, the chance to learn from senior brand leaders, and the opportunity to shape how Resmed shows up across global markets. You’ll grow your skills in brand strategy, cross functional collaboration, and brand governance at scale.
We are shaping the future at Resmed, and we recognize the need to build on and broaden our existing skills and continue to attract and retain the world’s best talent. We work hard to offer holistic benefits packages, provide flexible work arrangements, cultivate a workforce culture that allows employees to grow personally and professionally, and deliver competitive salaries to our team members.
